text:
Passive movements are movements of a body part produced by an external force—such as a therapist, machine, or gravity—rather than by the person's own muscle contraction. They are used in physical therapy and clinical assessment to maintain range of motion, prevent stiffness, and evaluate joint mobility or tone, and per the team note they are performed without resistance and stop at the end of the available range rather than stretching beyond it.
